items.title: Human Uniqueness Comes From Our Plasticity | John Dupre
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if human uniqueness comes from having less predetermined human nature?*

John Dupre argues that humans are uniquely plastic: our developmental flexibility allows individuals to acquire radically different skills, creating forms of cooperation and division of labor that no individual could achieve alone.

*John Dupré* is a British philosopher of science. He is the director of Egenis, the Centre for the Study of Life Sciences, and professor of philosophy at the University of Exeter. items.title: Acharya Prashant: Is Ego or Consciousness Fundamental? (Part 1)
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What is consciousness, and can we understand it without first asking who is conscious?*

In this extended conversation, Acharya Prashant and Robert Lawrence Kuhn bring Western philosophy of mind into dialogue with Vedantic traditions. They explore consciousness and the ego, physicalism and idealism, self-inquiry, karma and reincarnation, animal and artificial consciousness, free choice, and whether anything about human existence lies beyond the physical.

Their approaches converge at some points and sharply diverge at others—especially over what, if anything, is fundamental.

0:00 The Ego and Consciousness
0:56 Introduction to Acharya Prashant
2:31 Consciousness in the Vedic Traditions
10:21 Eastern and Western Views of Consciousness
18:26 The Physicality of Consciousness
28:20 Love, Suffering, and the Ego
36:58 Vedanta, Samkhya, and Liberation
41:51 Reincarnation and Life After Death
45:06 What Karma Really Means
50:21 How Religious Traditions Become Distorted
57:08 Vedanta Meets Western Philosophy of Mind
1:08:08 Idealism and Consciousness
1:23:28 The Boundaries of Consciousness
1:34:29 AI and Consciousness
1:36:14 The Ego as Fundamental
1:44:38 The Mystery of Choice and Love
1:50:33 God and the Dissolution of the Ego

*Acharya Prashant* is the founder of the PrashantAdvait Foundation and a teacher of Advaita Vedanta, the Indian philosophy of non-dual self-inquiry. His teachings on the Bhagavad Gita, the Upanishads, and the nature of the self have made him one of the most widely followed wisdom teachers today.

items.title: Can Scientific Change Be Darwinian? | Derek Turner
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could scientific change work something like biological evolution?*

Derek Turner explores an evolutionary analogy in which science can be viewed as a population of hypotheses and theories subjected to selection pressure, while asking whether gradual change and paradigm shifts resemble patterns found in biological evolution.

0:00 Evolutionary Theory and Cultural Change

*Derek Turner* is the Class of '43 Professor of Philosophy and Director of the Goodwin-Niering Center for the Environment at Connecticut College. A recipient of both the John S. King Teaching Award and the Nisbet Rash Research Award, his work focuses on the philosophy of paleontology, macroevolution, and deep time. He is the author of _Paleontology: A Philosophical Introduction_ and _Paleoaesthetics and the Practice of Paleontology,_ as well as a co-founder of the philosophy of paleontology blog _Extinct._

items.title: Can Neuroscience Fully Explain Understanding? | Gordon Graham
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could neuroscience explain everything the mind does and still miss what it means to understand?*

Gordon Graham argues that imagination, practical skill, and aesthetic understanding reveal a distinction between explaining the mechanisms of thought and judging its truth, value, or insight.

0:00 Art Offers Another View of the Mind-Body Problem
1:21 Imagination Does Not Depend on Correspondence
3:24 Prediction Does Not Establish Understanding
4:33 Scientific Imperialism and the Limits of Explanatory Promises

items.title: Does Human Agency Drive Progress? | Martin Seligman
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could a psychological belief help explain why entire civilizations flourish or stagnate?*

Martin Seligman extends his research on helplessness, optimism, and agency into history, examining whether changes in people's sense of control are associated with changes in human progress.

0:00 The Psychology of Human Agency
3:08 Agency and the Meaning of Progress
5:56 Reading the Minds of the Dead
15:26 Individual and Collective Agency in China
21:07 The Psychological Cost of Individual Agency
25:47 Agency and Modern Human Progress
29:41 AI, Deskilling, and Human Agency

*Martin E.P. Seligman* is the Zellerbach Family Professor of Psychology at the University of Pennsylvania and Director of the Penn Positive Psychology Center. A leading figure in positive psychology, his research focuses on well-being, resilience, learned helplessness, optimism, and depression.

items.title: Did Evolution Give Us a Sense of Oneness? | Helen De Cruz
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Why do humans across cultures experience a sense of oneness?*

Helen De Cruz traces ideas of interconnectedness from religious philosophy to early human social networks and our longstanding relationship with nature, suggesting that these experiences may remain embedded in our psychology.

0:00 Oneness Begins With Concrete Experience
2:28 Interconnectedness Runs Deep in Human History
3:51 Humans Were Interconnected With Nature, and Still Benefit From It

*Helen De Cruz* (1978–2025) was a Belgian philosopher and Danforth Chair in the Humanities at Saint Louis University. Their research focused on philosophy of religion, experimental philosophy, and cognitive science, exploring topics such as religious belief, wonder, and human reasoning.
